claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature toughness than commercially pure tungsten.
Severe lattice distortions are the primary cause of the HEA's enhanced high-temperature plastic strain and toughness.
Severe lattice distortions promote dynamic recovery in WTaTiVZr.
Severe lattice distortions facilitate more homogeneous, stress-relieved dislocation motion.
Dynamic recovery and homogeneous dislocation motion delay crack initiation and propagation during high-temperature loading.
The proposed HEA is equimolar WTaTiVZr, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each constituent.
The controlled comparison uses as-homogenized WTaTiVZr and commercially pure tungsten with similar grain sizes.
The comparison should hold environment, strain rate, temperature, grain size, and initial dislocation density constant.
The proposed tests are conducted at approximately 500–1000 °C in inert gas or vacuum.
Lattice distortions generate heterogeneous local stress fields in the HEA.
The local stress variations lower activation barriers for dislocation motion.
Pure tungsten has less capacity for dynamic recovery than WTaTiVZr under comparable high-temperature loading.
Reduced dynamic-recovery capacity in pure tungsten leads to dislocation pile-up and earlier crack initiation.
The HEA will show greater plastic deformation before fracture than pure tungsten.
The HEA will show higher fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
In-situ observations will show more dynamic recovery and altered dislocation behavior in the HEA than in pure tungsten.
Commercially pure tungsten is known to have limited ductility and toughness because of its relatively homogeneous structure and limitations on dislocation motion.
The hypothesis is limited to equimolar refractory-element HEAs tested at 500–1000 °C under low-oxidation conditions and may not generalize to other compositions, processing states, or temperatures.
Failure to observe statistically significant gains in plastic strain or toughness, or failure to observe enhanced dynamic recovery and altered dislocation mechanisms, would falsify the hypothesis.
